description: Normalization (Pydantic default-filling via JewelryDefinition.model_validate()) never changes design intent — it only fills omitted fields with their documented defaults. Reused from specs/jdl/v1/test-vectors/definition-hash-vectors.json (Sprint 3), generated by running the real implementation.

vectors.name: minimal-input-normalizes-to-default
vectors.note: An authored document with every field omitted except schemaVersion normalizes to byte-identical canonical JSON as the fully-explicit default document — proof that normalization adds defaults, never invents or alters a value the author actually provided.

vectors.name: explicit-default-values-are-unchanged
vectors.note: Explicitly restating the default values produces the identical hash — normalization is idempotent.

vectors.name: normalization-does-not-fix-invalid-values
vectors.note: A negative band.width passes structurally through normalization unchanged (Pydantic has no positivity constraint on this field — see specs/jdl/v1/jdl.schema.json) and is only later rejected by Forge semantic validation (JM-BAND-001, JM-GEOMETRY-001). Normalization never silently clamps or fixes it.

currentImplementation: backend/jewelmind/domain/schema.py::JewelryDefinition.model_validate() is the entire current normalization step — no separate 'normalization stage' function exists; Pydantic's own default-filling and type coercion (strict mode) is the full extent of it.
